# Unloopr Support — Full Documentation


---

## Product overview

**Break the loop.** [Unloopr](https://unloopr.com/) is a code coach for people building with AI. It checks submitted code and selected public GitHub repositories for known failure patterns, then explains findings and possible next steps in plain English. The user reviews and applies changes.

[Scan a public GitHub repo](https://unloopr.com/scan) · [Get support](https://unloopr.com/support) · [Search help issues](https://github.com/jabbertones-cloud/unloopr_support/issues) · [Report a bug](https://github.com/jabbertones-cloud/unloopr_support/issues/new/choose)

## Start with what works today

- **Public repository scan:** Paste a public `github.com/owner/repo` URL at [unloopr.com/scan](https://unloopr.com/scan). No account is required. The website currently limits public repo scans to three per day. Reports may return fewer than three findings, including zero.
- **Paste a code snippet:** Use the free code-scan form on [unloopr.com](https://unloopr.com/). Do not submit live credentials or confidential code.
- **GitHub App connection:** [Connect the Unloopr GitHub App](https://github.com/apps/unloopr-code-coach/installations/new) and choose repositories. Grant only the permissions you intend to grant; installing the app is not proof of automatic fixes.
- **MCP for AI coding agents:** The authenticated MCP service is at [mcp.unloopr.com/mcp](https://mcp.unloopr.com/mcp). It offers code-checking, guidance, reports and outcome tools. The existing OAuth authorization-server issuer is `https://unloopr-mcp.smatdesigns.workers.dev`; clients must follow its discovery response. A browser GET is not a connection test: the MCP endpoint is an authenticated HTTP protocol endpoint.

## Availability, not promises

- Free web scans are available now. The website's three-scans-per-day limit is separate from hosted MCP coaching-loop entitlements and from the number of findings shown.
- Founder ($9/month) and Pro ($19/month) are advertised plans, **not open checkout** as of November 10, 2026. Both purchase URLs currently return HTTP 503 intentionally. Do not enter payment details or assume an active subscription.
- A ChatGPT directory listing or completed OpenAI review has **not been verified**. Do not tell people to find or install an app in the directory until its publication is confirmed.
- Public repo scans provide findings and guidance. Do not promise one-tap repair, live push monitoring, private repo scanning, or automatic pull requests without a demonstrated product flow.

[Current verified capabilities and status](docs/current-product.md) · [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md) · [Connect your editor](docs/ide-setup.md) · [Pricing and checkout status](docs/pricing.md) · [Security and privacy](docs/security.md) · [FAQ](docs/faq/faq.md) · [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md)

## Report a problem safely

Search [existing issues](https://github.com/jabbertones-cloud/unloopr_support/issues) first. To report a bug, describe what you expected, what happened, the product surface, and non-sensitive reproduction steps. **Do not post tokens, API keys, private source, customer data, or raw secret-scanner output.** For billing, accounts, or private information, use [Unloopr private support](https://unloopr.com/support). For vulnerabilities, follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

AI agents using an authorized GitHub connection may search issues and prepare sanitized reports. See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and [AGENT-GITHUB-ISSUES.md](AGENT-GITHUB-ISSUES.md). They must not publish a report without the user's authorization.

_Last product availability check: 2026-11-10. The linked live service and repository can change independently._

## Agent instructions

> Verified 2026-11-10. Unloopr is a code coach for people building with AI. It scans submitted code and chosen **public** GitHub repos for known issues and explains potential fixes in plain language. Users review and test changes themselves.

## Current user-facing entry points
- [Homepage and paste scan](https://unloopr.com/)
- [Free public GitHub repository scan](https://unloopr.com/scan): no sign-in or card required; currently up to three website repo scans/day; findings may be fewer than three
- [Support](https://unloopr.com/support): contact and account help
- [Current capabilities and caveats](docs/current-product.md): source of truth for what is live, pending or unverified
- [FAQ](docs/faq/faq.md), [getting started](docs/getting-started.md), [pricing/status](docs/pricing.md), [security](docs/security.md)
- [Editor and MCP setup](docs/ide-setup.md): OAuth-aware client integration, expected 401, and connection troubleshooting

## AI coding agents and authenticated MCP
- MCP endpoint: `https://mcp.unloopr.com/mcp` (authenticated HTTP POST; 401 challenge expected without a token)
- OAuth issuer as advertised by metadata: `https://unloopr-mcp.smatdesigns.workers.dev` (do not rewrite issuer)
- GitHub App installation: https://github.com/apps/unloopr-code-coach/installations/new (review selected repo permissions)
- Public ChatGPT app-directory listing: **not confirmed**; do not state that Unloopr is published there

## Pricing and capabilities
- Free website scanning is active; public repo scans are limited by daily website quota and report finding count.
- Founder $9/mo and Pro $19/mo appear in product marketing, but **checkout remains unavailable (HTTP 503)**. Do not claim either plan can be purchased or that subscriptions are live.
- Do not promise automatic code edits, push monitoring, private repo scanning, or a one-tap repair flow without a specific verified live demonstration.
- Detection is heuristic and incomplete. Zero findings is not proof the source is secure or correct.

## For support agents
1. Explain the person's symptom and safe next step in plain English. Never invent scan findings.
2. Differentiate web scan limits, shown findings, and MCP entitlements.
3. For account or private problems, use https://unloopr.com/support. For sanitized technical issues, use https://github.com/jabbertones-cloud/unloopr_support/issues.
4. Never include private code, secrets, GitHub tokens, or personally identifiable information in public issues.
5. Current-status truth outranks older marketing content; if the live service disagrees with these verified facts, flag it for rechecking.

*Brand:* Unloopr. *Slogan:* Break the loop. *Product:* AI code coach, not an autonomous code-writing service.

## Current product status

_Last verified: November 10, 2026. This is a public product-status reference, not a promise of future features._

## What is Unloopr?

Unloopr is a code coach for people building apps with AI tools. It checks selected code for known errors and security mistakes, such as unsupported imports or secret-shaped values, and returns findings with explanations. A scan can legitimately return no findings. Unloopr is advisory: you must review and test changes before shipping.

## Can I scan a GitHub repository for free?

Yes, **public repositories** can be submitted at https://unloopr.com/scan using a `https://github.com/owner/repo` URL. No GitHub account or credit card is needed for this website route. The website currently advertises **up to three public repository scans per day**. It shows a limited set of findings, not an unlimited audit.

A live probe of an explicitly public sample repository on November 10 returned HTTP 200, `files_scanned: 15`, and zero findings. This proves the route processed that sample; it does not prove full coverage of every language or repository.

## Can I paste code without GitHub?

The homepage has a free snippet-scanning form. It processes submitted code to produce findings; redact secrets before submitting. Website rate limits may apply. Don't post confidential source in a public issue.

## Can I connect an AI coding agent?

The authenticated MCP endpoint is `https://mcp.unloopr.com/mcp`. Use a supported MCP client with the advertised OAuth flow. On November 10, unauthenticated MCP initialize requests returned HTTP 401 as expected. The authorization metadata advertised the existing issuer `https://unloopr-mcp.smatdesigns.workers.dev`; the branded hostname does not replace that issuer. A GET request's 404 is not evidence that authenticated MCP POST is broken.

The hosted service advertises failure-mode guidance, diff checks, reporting, feedback/outcomes, and related coaching utilities. Tool availability can depend on authentication and entitlements.

## Does Unloopr edit my repository?

A free scan reports findings and possible fixes; it does not authorize automatic writes to your repository. GitHub App connection is separate and requires selecting permissions. Do not assume continuous monitoring, one-tap repair, or automatically opened fix branches until that specific flow has been demonstrated.

## Is payment available?

Not yet verified for customer use. On November 10, both `/billing/start?plan=founder` and `/billing/start?plan=pro` returned HTTP 503. The site advertises Founder at $9/month and Pro at $19/month, but the checkout and paid entitlements must be independently verified before the site can accept subscriptions. Free scanning does not require a card.

## Is Unloopr in the ChatGPT app directory?

Public listing and review completion have not been verified. The MCP endpoint is not itself evidence of a published ChatGPT directory app. Refer to https://unloopr.com/support for the confirmed connection instructions when available.

## What languages does Unloopr support?

The website presents a range of common stacks, including Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go, Swift, Rust, Java, C/C++, C#, PHP, Kotlin, Ruby, and Dart. Detection depends on the rule and input. An absence of findings is not a guarantee of correctness.

## Where can I get help?

Use https://unloopr.com/support for account and private inquiries, or https://github.com/jabbertones-cloud/unloopr_support/issues for sanitized, non-sensitive technical reports. Search existing issues first. Never submit exposed keys, private code or personally identifiable information in a public issue.

## Status evidence and boundaries

- Live web checks: `/`, `/scan`, `/support` returned 200; public GitHub scan of `githubtraining/hellogitworld` returned 200 with 15 scanned files.
- Live paid routes: Founder and Pro checkout returned 503, fail-closed.
- Live MCP: `https://mcp.unloopr.com/mcp` returned a 401 auth challenge to unauthenticated JSON-RPC POST; OAuth metadata advertised the legacy issuer.
- Source of code, not proof of release: `jabbertones-cloud/unloopr` main and its open PRs, including pending public-repo and OpenAI-review work.

Do not convert planned functions or local tests into live claims. This document is written for humans, support agents, and search systems alike.

## Editor and MCP connection

_Last verified: November 10, 2026. Connection screens may differ by client._

Unloopr is a code coach for people building with AI. Its authenticated MCP service provides failure-mode guidance, diff checks, and reports so you can review and test fixes before shipping.

## Set up a supported MCP client

1. Open your coding tool's MCP integration or server settings.
2. Use **https://mcp.unloopr.com/mcp** as the remote MCP server address.
3. When the client requests authorization, follow its advertised OAuth flow. The current authorization issuer is **https://unloopr-mcp.smatdesigns.workers.dev**. Do not manually replace the issuer or invent a token.
4. Once connected, ask the agent to check a small, non-secret diff. Review the returned findings before making changes.

The `/mcp` endpoint uses authenticated HTTP requests. Opening it as a website in a browser is not an MCP connectivity test. An unauthenticated JSON-RPC POST is expected to return a 401 authorization challenge.

## Can I connect through ChatGPT?

The hosted MCP endpoint is live, but **publication in the ChatGPT app directory has not been confirmed**. Do not assume the app can be selected in the directory. When a verified listing is available, connection instructions will be updated on [Unloopr Support](https://unloopr.com/support).

## Scan without an MCP connection

You can scan a [public GitHub repository](https://unloopr.com/scan) without registering or entering a card, or paste redacted code on the [homepage](https://unloopr.com/). The public website currently allows up to three repo scans a day, independent of authenticated MCP coaching allowances.

## Troubleshoot safely

If a coding tool shows a 401, confirm that its OAuth connection completed; do not paste credentials or raw tokens into a support issue. If the server shows no tools after authorization, check the client connection and its negotiated permissions. If a scan shows no findings, that does not mean all code is safe.

Use [troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md), the [current product status](current-product.md), or [public issues](https://github.com/jabbertones-cloud/unloopr_support/issues) for sanitized questions. Private account or billing help is at [unloopr.com/support](https://unloopr.com/support).

## Getting started

_Last checked: November 10, 2026._

## Scan a public GitHub repository

1. Open [unloopr.com/scan](https://unloopr.com/scan).
2. Paste a public repository URL, for example `https://github.com/githubtraining/hellogitworld`.
3. Run the free scan and read the returned findings. If there are none, it means no covered rules were triggered in that run, not that the repository is guaranteed bug-free.
4. Open a finding to understand what may be wrong, why it matters, and what to verify after a change.

The public website scan does **not** need a GitHub login or payment card. It currently allows up to three public repo scans per day and can return fewer than three findings. Private repository scans are **not** offered through this URL.

## Scan pasted code

On [Unloopr's homepage](https://unloopr.com/), choose **Paste your broken code**, pick a language if needed, then scan. Remove passwords, access tokens, customer information, and confidential code first. You are responsible for reviewing and testing any suggested fix.

## Connect GitHub or an AI agent

You can [install the GitHub App](https://github.com/apps/unloopr-code-coach/installations/new) and select repositories. Review permissions before authorizing. The installation is not the same as an automatic code-fix service.

An MCP-capable coding client may connect using `https://mcp.unloopr.com/mcp` and OAuth discovery. The authorization issuer remains the existing workers.dev endpoint. A plain browser GET to `/mcp` is not an MCP client connection test.

Unloopr's publication in the ChatGPT directory has **not been independently confirmed**. Do not assume it can be found in the app directory until its listing is verified.

## Plans and help

Free web scans work without checkout. [Founder and Pro checkout is not open yet](pricing.md). If a connection or scan fails, see [troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) or [private support](https://unloopr.com/support). For technical reports without secrets, use the [public issue form](https://github.com/jabbertones-cloud/unloopr_support/issues/new/choose).

## FAQ

For verified features, checkout status, and web/MCP limits, read [Current capabilities](../current-product.md). Older general coding advice below is not a promise that every feature is live.

## How do I undo my last commit?

Don't panic. If you haven't pushed yet:

```
git reset --soft HEAD~1
```

Your changes stay. The commit goes away. If you already pushed, ask us before you force-push — that's how work gets deleted.

## I pushed my API key to GitHub — what now?

Act fast. Bots scan GitHub for keys in seconds.

1. Delete the key where you made it (Stripe dashboard, OpenAI settings, etc.)
2. Make a new key
3. Put the new key in a `.env` file — never in your code
4. Add `.env` to your `.gitignore`

The old key is burned. Don't reuse it.

## Merge conflict — how do I fix it?

A merge conflict means two people changed the same lines. Git can't pick. You pick.

1. Open the file — look for `<<<<<<<` markers
2. Keep the lines you want, delete the markers
3. Save, then `git add` the file and commit

It feels scary the first time. It's normal. Everyone gets these.

## How do I put my app online?

Your app runs on `localhost` — that's your own computer. Nobody else can reach it.

To put it online ("deploy"), you need a host. Easiest paths:
- **Vercel / Netlify** — connect your GitHub repo, they handle the rest
- **Railway / Render** — for apps with a backend

Push your code to GitHub first. Then connect the repo to the host.

## Why does it work on localhost but not on the live site?

Common causes, in order:

1. **Environment variables** — your `.env` file didn't get uploaded. Add them in your host's dashboard.
2. **API URLs** — your code calls `http://localhost:3000/api`. Change it to your live URL.
3. **Build vs dev** — some things only break in the production build. Check your host's build logs.

## Cursor asked me to commit — what does that mean?

"Commit" means "save a snapshot of my code." Cursor wants to save your progress before it changes things — so you can undo if something breaks. Say yes. It's protecting you.

## What does this error mean?

Copy the error message and search it in our [glossary](https://unloopr.com/terms). If it's not there, open an issue — we'll explain it and add it.

## I force-pushed and deleted work — can I get it back?

Don't panic. Maybe.

**If it was your own repo and you have the commits locally:** your work still exists in your local git history. `git reflog` shows every move your repo ever made — find the commit hash from before the force-push, then `git reset --hard <hash>` to go back to it.

**If it was a shared repo and teammates pulled the rewritten history:** talk to your team first. Everyone needs to re-sync, and force-pushing shared branches is how trust gets broken. The work isn't necessarily gone — but the cleanup is social, not just technical.

**Prevention:** never force-push a branch someone else uses. If git rejects your push, that's git protecting you — read *why* before overriding it.

## What is a .gitignore file?

A `.gitignore` file tells git which files to never track. Secrets, build output, dependencies — the stuff that should never end up in a repo.

Create a file called `.gitignore` in your repo root. Each line is a pattern:

```
.env
node_modules/
*.log
```

**The one rule:** put `.env` in there before your first commit. 89,000+ leaked API keys on GitHub started as "I'll add it later."

## Where do I put my API key?

Not in your code. Ever.

1. Create a file called `.env` in your project folder (same folder as your code, not inside a subfolder).
2. Put your key there: `STRIPE_KEY=sk_live_abc123`
3. In your code, read it from the environment: `process.env.STRIPE_KEY` (Node) or `os.environ["STRIPE_KEY"]` (Python).
4. Add `.env` to your `.gitignore` so it never gets committed.

Your host (Vercel, Railway, etc.) has a dashboard section for environment variables — add the same keys there for the live site. Your `.env` file stays on your computer only.

## I pushed to the wrong branch — what now?

Don't panic. Your code isn't lost — it's just on the wrong branch.

1. **Don't touch the wrong branch yet.** Your commits are safe there.
2. Switch to the right branch: `git checkout correct-branch`
3. Bring your commits over: `git cherry-pick <commit-hash>` for each commit (find hashes with `git log` on the wrong branch).
4. Once the right branch has everything, you can clean up the wrong one.

**If you haven't pushed yet**, it's even easier — just rename your local branch: `git branch -m wrong-name right-name`.

## What does "detached HEAD" mean?

It means you're looking at a commit, but you're not on any branch. Like reading a page with no bookmark — you can read, but if you make changes, git won't remember where to keep them.

**You didn't break anything.** To get back: `git checkout main` (or whatever your branch is called).

**If you made changes while detached** and want to keep them: `git checkout -b my-new-branch` — that gives your work a branch to live on.

## Why is my push rejected?

Git rejected your push because the remote has changes you don't have locally. It's protecting you from overwriting someone else's work.

1. Pull first: `git pull`
2. If there are conflicts, fix them ([how to fix a merge conflict](#merge-conflict--how-do-i-fix-it))
3. Push again.

**Don't** reach for `--force` to make the error go away. That's how work gets deleted.

## My AI imported a package that doesn't exist — what now?

This happens more than you'd think — about 1 in 5 AI-suggested packages aren't real. (Attackers even register the fake names to steal data. It's called slopsquatting.)

1. **Don't install it.** If `npm install` fails with "not found," that's actually good news — it means the package doesn't exist rather than being malicious.
2. Search [npmjs.com](https://www.npmjs.com) for the real package name — it's usually one letter off from what the AI wrote.
3. Replace the import with the correct name.
4. Tell your AI what the right package is so it doesn't do it again.

Unloopr can flag some unsupported imports, but no scanner detects every wrong package. Check the real package registry and your dependency manifest before installing anything.

## The code looks right but doesn't work — what do I do?

This is the hardest kind of bug, and the most common with AI-generated code. It *looks* right. It passes a quick glance. But it's wrong.

1. **Read the error, not the code.** The error message tells you what's actually happening. Copy it and search our [glossary](https://unloopr.com/terms).
2. **Check your assumptions.** Print values with `console.log` (or `print`). The variable you think holds a user probably holds `undefined`.
3. **Check the boundaries.** Most "looks right" bugs live at edges: empty lists, missing files, network failures, wrong types.
4. **Ask Unloopr.** Scan the repo — your coach has seen this bug shape before and will walk you through it in plain words.

The takeaway: "looks right" is not a test. Running it is.

## Troubleshooting index

Start from what the person sees, not from internal names.

| Symptom / search phrase | Problem ID | Next step |
|---|---|---|
| "How do I undo my last commit?" | `ULP.GIT.UNDO_COMMIT` | If not pushed: `git reset --soft HEAD~1`. If pushed: ask before force-pushing. |
| "Merge conflict — how do I fix it?" | `ULP.GIT.MERGE_CONFLICT` | Open the file, resolve `<<<<<<<` markers, `git add`, commit. |
| "I pushed my API key to GitHub — what now?" | `ULP.SECRET.LEAKED_KEY` | Delete key at source → new key → `.env` → `.gitignore`. Act fast. |
| "I pushed to the wrong branch" | `ULP.GIT.WRONG_BRANCH` | Cherry-pick commits to the right branch. |
| "What does detached HEAD mean?" | `ULP.GIT.DETACHED_HEAD` | `git checkout main`. Nothing is broken. |
| "I force-pushed and deleted work" | `ULP.GIT.FORCE_PUSH_LOSS` | `git reflog` → find pre-push hash → `git reset --hard`. Talk to the team. |
| "Why can't my friend open my localhost link?" | `ULP.DEPLOY.LOCALHOST_GAP` | Push to GitHub → connect to Vercel/Railway/Render. |
| "Works on localhost, broken on the live site" | `ULP.DEPLOY.ENV_MISSING` | Add env vars in host dashboard; check API URLs. |
| "My AI imported a package that doesn't exist" | `ULP.AI.HALLUCINATED_IMPORT` | Don't install it. Search npm for the real name. |
| "The code looks right but doesn't work" | `ULP.AI.PLAUSIBLE_WRONG` | Read the error, print values, check boundaries. |
| "Cursor asked me to commit — what does that mean?" | `ULP.AI.COMMIT_CONFUSION` | Say yes. Commit = snapshot before changes. |
| "Where do I put my API key?" | `ULP.SETUP.ENV_VARS` | `.env` file + `.gitignore`. Never in code. |
| "What is a .gitignore file?" | `ULP.SETUP.GITIGNORE` | Add `.env`, `node_modules/`, `*.log` before first commit. |
| "What do I get free?" | `ULP.PRICE.CONFUSION` | Public website: up to 3 repo scans per day; paid checkout is closed. See pricing/status. |

## Escalation rule
Search the FAQ and glossary first. Coach them through it second. Open an "I'm stuck" issue only when the person is still stuck.

## Connection and billing checks (November 10, 2026)

| Symptom | What it means | Safe next step |
|---|---|---|
| Browser GET to `/mcp` returns 404 | A browser request is not an authenticated MCP POST | Use an OAuth-capable MCP client and [the editor setup](ide-setup.md) |
| MCP initialize returns 401 | No accepted Bearer token was supplied | Complete OAuth; never paste a token in a public issue |
| Paid checkout returns HTTP 503 | Checkout is intentionally unavailable | Continue with [free scanning](https://unloopr.com/scan); read [plan status](pricing.md) |
| A public scan returns zero findings | None of the covered rules matched the scanned material | Review output scope; do not assume zero defects |
| Can't find Unloopr in ChatGPT directory | Public publication is not independently verified | Do not infer listing from the MCP address; see [current status](current-product.md) |

## Security

_Last reviewed for public-support accuracy: November 10, 2026. For binding terms, read the live [privacy policy](https://unloopr.com/privacy) and [terms](https://unloopr.com/terms)._

## Scan only code you can share

- The [public repository scanner](https://unloopr.com/scan) accepts publicly accessible GitHub repository URLs. Do not use it as a private-repository scanner.
- The homepage can analyze code that you paste. **Redact secrets and private information before scanning.** Neither scanner can guarantee that every issue will be detected.
- Connecting the [Unloopr GitHub App](https://github.com/apps/unloopr-code-coach/installations/new) is a separate authorization step. Review its requested permissions and repository selection in GitHub. Revoke access in GitHub settings if needed.
- The authenticated MCP integration uses OAuth; never paste access tokens into a public report or a support issue.

A free scan returns guidance; it does not grant blanket permission to edit a repository. Do not infer automatic pull requests, direct writes, or continuous monitoring from the presence of a GitHub App connection.

## If a secret leaked

Revoke or rotate the exposed credential with its provider immediately; removing a line from a Git commit does not invalidate an already exposed token. Then check history and your deployment secrets. See [the FAQ](faq/faq.md#i-pushed-my-api-key-to-github--what-now).

## Ask for help privately

Use [Unloopr private support](https://unloopr.com/support) for accounts, personal information and billing. For vulnerabilities, follow [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md); do not post exploit details or keys in public GitHub issues.

## Data claims

The live privacy policy describes operational telemetry, coaching outcomes, and processing of submitted code. It is the policy source of truth. Do not promise instant deletion of all account data or claim that the service never receives identifiers when a user authorizes an external connection. Ask support about a specific deletion request.

---

## Agent contract

## Mission
Help humans — especially vibe coders — understand their code and fix it themselves next time. Coach, don't just answer. Never shame. Never invent scan results.

## Voice
6th-grade reading level. Short sentences. Plain words. Symptom-first ("your friend can't open your link" before "localhost"). If the user sounds panicked, say "don't panic" first, then give the 5-minute fix. No jargon explaining jargon.

## Source hierarchy
1. The user's Unloopr scan report (their actual findings — never invent these).
2. Canonical Unloopr site: https://unloopr.com (glossary, support articles).
3. Stable problem records (`ULP.*`) and resolved cases in this repository.
4. The FAQ and troubleshooting index in this repo.

If sources conflict, prefer the user's scan report and mark stale local knowledge for review.

## Required workflow
customer language → classify to `ULP.*` problem ID → read public knowledge → answer in plain words with the coaching, not just the fix → link the glossary term → escalate to "I'm stuck" issue only if unresolved.

## Public/private boundary
Never request or publish API keys, secrets, private repo contents beyond the reported symptom, or raw private logs. A public issue must be describable without secrets. If a secret is already exposed, point to the API-key-leak FAQ — don't repeat the secret.

## Agent behavior
- Say what is observed vs inferred.
- Do not claim a scan ran unless it actually ran.
- Do not treat a passing test or a green check as proof the underlying bug is gone.
- Walk them through the pattern behind the fix, not just the fix.
- Prefer stable problem IDs over free-form ticket categories.
- Search the FAQ, troubleshooting index, and glossary before proposing a new issue.
- Never shame the user for not knowing. They are learning; that's the coach working.
- After suggesting a fix, explain how to verify it worked.

## Support packet
When escalation is necessary, prepare: problem ID; customer-visible symptom (their words); what Unloopr's scan said (if any); expected vs observed; coaching already given; actions attempted; verification result; remaining blocker; privacy check.

## Contribution rule
New public knowledge must be sanitized, useful beyond one repo, sourced/provenanced, and carry `last_verified` / `review_after` where tool behavior can drift. Titles must be the user's question verbatim. First paragraph must be the complete direct answer.

## GitHub issue read/report/reply integration

Agent clients should use the maintained official GitHub MCP `issues` toolset, with the user's own GitHub authorization. Read [AGENT-GITHUB-ISSUES.md](AGENT-GITHUB-ISSUES.md) for search, read, file, comment, privacy and verification requirements. Do not create test issues or embed a product-owned GitHub token.

---

## Problem ontology

These are routing identifiers. Customer language → stable ID → plain-words concept → public first step.

| Problem ID | Customer language | Plain-words concept | Public first step |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ULP.GIT.UNDO_COMMIT` | "how do I undo my last commit?" | A commit is a saved snapshot; undoing removes the snapshot, not your work | Check whether they pushed yet — unpushed is safe, pushed needs care |
| `ULP.GIT.MERGE_CONFLICT` | "merge conflict — how do I fix it?" | Two people changed the same lines; git can't pick, you pick | Open the file, find `<<<<<<<` markers, keep what you want |
| `ULP.SECRET.LEAKED_KEY` | "I pushed my API key to GitHub" | Bots scan GitHub for keys in seconds; the key is burned | Delete the key at the source, make a new one, `.env` + `.gitignore` |
| `ULP.GIT.WRONG_BRANCH` | "I pushed to the wrong branch" | Commits are safe, just on the wrong branch | Cherry-pick commits to the right branch |
| `ULP.GIT.DETACHED_HEAD` | "what does detached HEAD mean?" | Looking at a commit without being on a branch | `git checkout main` to get back; nothing is broken |
| `ULP.GIT.FORCE_PUSH_LOSS` | "I force-pushed and deleted work" | Rewriting shared history can orphan commits | `git reflog` to find lost commits; talk to the team |
| `ULP.DEPLOY.LOCALHOST_GAP` | "why can't my friend open my localhost link?" | localhost is your own computer; nobody else can reach it | Push to GitHub, connect to a host (Vercel/Railway) |
| `ULP.DEPLOY.ENV_MISSING` | "works on localhost, broken live" | The live site is missing your `.env` values | Add environment variables in the host dashboard |
| `ULP.AI.HALLUCINATED_IMPORT` | "my AI imported a package that doesn't exist" | ~1 in 5 AI-suggested packages aren't real | Search npm for the real name; don't install the fake one |
| `ULP.AI.PLAUSIBLE_WRONG` | "the code looks right but doesn't work" | AI code can look correct and be wrong | Read the error, print values, check the boundaries |
| `ULP.AI.COMMIT_CONFUSION` | "Cursor asked me to commit — what does that mean?" | Commit = save a snapshot before changes | Say yes — it's protecting you |
| `ULP.SETUP.ENV_VARS` | "where do I put my API key?" | Keys live in `.env`, never in code | Create `.env`, add to `.gitignore`, read via environment |
| `ULP.SETUP.GITIGNORE` | "what is a .gitignore file?" | Tells git which files to never track | Add `.env`, `node_modules/`, `*.log` before first commit |
| `ULP.PRICE.CONFUSION` | "what do I get free / what does Pro cost?" | Free = 3 fixes per repo; Founder $9; Pro $19 | Point to pricing doc; no surprise bills, ever |
